beats.text: In 1835, the Mexican army came to take back a small *cannon* from the town of Gonzales.
The settlers made a flag with a picture of the cannon and two words, "Come and take it."
That was the start of the Texas *Revolution*.
Mexico's president, General Antonio López de Santa Anna, marched north with thousands of soldiers to crush it.
In February 1836, he reached San Antonio.
Inside the old mission, the Alamo, were around 200 Texan defenders, including a frontier celebrity named Davy Crockett.
They held out for *13* days.
On the morning of March the 6th, 1836, the Alamo fell.
Nearly every defender was killed.
Hundreds of Mexican soldiers died, too.
But Santa Anna had made a *mistake*.
He had given the Texans a battle cry, and then he made a second one.
He split up his army to chase them and pushed ahead with only part of it.
Four days before the Alamo fell, Texan delegates had already declared
independence, and on April the 21st, 1836, at San Jacinto, Sam Houston's army caught
Santa Anna's camp during the afternoon rest.
"Remember the *Alamo*!"
The battle lasted about *18* minutes.
Santa Anna was captured the next day, hiding in the *grass*.
To get his freedom, he signed away Texas.
